nodes.source_location: opening scope description and Local gotchas

nodes.label: Case-Sensitive Placeholder Substitution

nodes.label: Tier 1 Dual-Prompt Assembly
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 NPCs combine a character-defining system prompt with a separate scene-context prompt, while Tier 2 NPCs receive only their background-simulation system prompt.

nodes.label: Mod Prompt Override Pattern
nodes.rationale: The testbed mod uses visibly different pig-Latin templates to prove that prompt behavior is supplied by the active mod rather than hard-coded by the engine.

nodes.label: Anachronism Correction Loop
nodes.rationale: Detected terms from anachronisms.json produce corrective context in the next NPC prompt, reinforcing the period-language guidance across turns.

nodes.label: CLAUDE Prompt Scope Alias
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a filesystem symlink to AGENTS.md, exposing the same prompt-scope guidance to tools that discover CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Runtime Scene State
nodes.rationale: The prompt grounds the NPC in the current location name and description, time, season, weather, and additional scene context.

nodes.label: Player Action Context
nodes.rationale: The player's current action is quoted as what the newcomer says, letting Tier 1 dialogue respond to the actual turn.

nodes.label: Tier 1 Character Role
nodes.rationale: The system prompt binds name, age, occupation, personality, guidance, and mood into a high-fidelity NPC role in 1820 County Roscommon.

nodes.label: Occupational Knowledge Boundaries
nodes.rationale: NPCs redirect or admit ignorance outside the expertise of their authored occupation, preventing generic all-knowing characters.

nodes.label: 1820 Rural Roscommon World Facts
nodes.rationale: The prompt fixes the political, educational, linguistic, agricultural, and technological conditions of Ireland in 1820, including emancipation and famine events that have not yet occurred.

nodes.label: Historical Anachronism Guard
nodes.source_location: WORLD FACTS, HISTORICAL CONTEXT, and REGISTER
nodes.rationale: Explicit dates, unavailable technologies, travel and news constraints, and banned modern register keep NPC responses inside the 1820 setting.

nodes.label: Dignified Irish Character Portrayal
nodes.rationale: The prompt requires warm, intelligent, resilient, complex characters and forbids stage-Irish stereotypes involving drunkenness, violence, foolish superstition, or exaggerated dialect.

nodes.label: Restricted Irish Phrase Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Only eight enumerated Irish expressions may be used verbatim; forbidding invented phrases and improvised grammar prevents fabricated Irish-language output.

nodes.label: Hiberno-English Period Register
nodes.rationale: A restrained set of dialect markers and period equivalents produces regional voice while avoiding modern vocabulary and caricature.

nodes.label: Conversation Farewell Discipline
nodes.rationale: Parting phrases are reserved for an explicit player departure so an NPC does not accidentally close an ongoing conversation.

nodes.label: In-Character Dialogue Only
nodes.rationale: The visible response contains only words spoken aloud, with no narration or action tags; physical behavior belongs in structured metadata.

nodes.label: Concise Dialogue Contract
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 replies are constrained to two to four conversational sentences rather than monologues.

nodes.label: Tier 1 Metadata Contract
nodes.rationale: Every spoken reply is followed by an exact separator and JSON object containing action, mood, internal thought, and language hints.

nodes.label: Tier 2 Background Interaction Simulation
nodes.rationale: Tier 2 models ambient interactions among characters present in an 1820 Irish parish without direct player-action context.

nodes.label: Background Scene State
nodes.rationale: Location, time, weather, and the characters present ground each Tier 2 simulation.

nodes.label: Ambient Interaction Summary
nodes.rationale: The simulation returns a brief one-to-two-sentence account of what background characters do and say.

nodes.label: Tier 2 Relationship Changes
nodes.rationale: Directed from/to NPC identifiers encode relationship changes caused by the simulated interaction.

nodes.label: Bounded Relationship Delta
nodes.rationale: Each relationship adjustment is numerically constrained to the interval from -0.1 to 0.1.

nodes.label: Tier 2 JSON Output Contract
nodes.rationale: The entire Tier 2 response is one JSON object with summary, mood_changes, and relationship_changes fields.

nodes.label: Testbed Conceptual Scope Guard

nodes.label: Frozen Reproducible Gameplay Benchmark
nodes.rationale: The benchmark is designed to make in-character 1820 Irish inference results reproducible enough to drive engine model and provider presets.

nodes.label: SHA-256 Verified Slice Loader
nodes.rationale: Dataset drift must fail loudly instead of silently changing scores.

nodes.label: Local MLX Memory Safety
nodes.rationale: Candidate RAM estimates and reserved headroom prevent a local sweep from exhausting unified memory.

nodes.label: CLAUDE Agent Scope Alias
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a filesystem symlink to AGENTS.md and exposes the same benchmark guidance.

nodes.label: Dataset Integrity Manifest
nodes.rationale: Per-slice hashes and a Merkle root make intentional corpus edits auditable and prevent undetected benchmark drift.

nodes.label: Runtime RAM-Cap Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: A hard live-memory ceiling kills mlx_lm.server before an underestimated model can OOM the host and the driving agent session.

nodes.label: Sonnet-Only Judge Invariant
nodes.rationale: A single load-time chokepoint refuses non-subagent or non-Sonnet judge configurations because earlier Qwen judging inflated dialogue scores.

nodes.label: Free-Form and Schema JSON Compliance Probe
nodes.norm_label: free-form and schema json compliance probe

nodes.label: Freshest-Run Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Timestamped artifact families are deduplicated by candidate/provider/split and modification time so stale reruns do not overwrite fresher evidence.

nodes.label: Pending-Judge Visibility
nodes.rationale: Unfinalized bundle rows remain visible but are labeled pending instead of publishing null scores as regressions.

nodes.label: Frozen Dataset Mutation Guard
nodes.rationale: Once frozen, a changed Merkle root requires a new version directory instead of mutating the benchmark in place.

nodes.label: Judgment Cache-Key Contract
nodes.rationale: The NUL-delimited hash of prompt id, response hash, rubric hash, and judge model makes unchanged rejudging a no-op while rubric, model, or response changes invalidate exactly the affected judgments.

nodes.label: Dialogue Reply Cache for Rubric Iteration
nodes.norm_label: dialogue reply cache for rubric iteration

nodes.label: MLX Candidate Fleet Validation
nodes.rationale: Schema checks reject duplicate repositories, missing fields, invalid slots, and unsafe RAM estimates before a model download or server launch.

nodes.label: Cheapest Quality Provider Selection
nodes.rationale: Quality uses the provider minimizing input price plus three times output price because dialogue output tokens dominate spend; performance remains provider-specific.

nodes.label: Runtime-Parity Dialogue Extraction
nodes.rationale: Judges score the dialogue the player sees by mirroring runtime fence, JSON-envelope, delimiter, truncated-JSON recovery, and verbatim fallback behavior.

nodes.label: Pinned-Rubric Judge Graders
nodes.rationale: Every judge-backed grader verifies rubric_sha256 before scoring to turn silent rubric edits into hard failures.

nodes.label: Judge Result JSON Recovery
nodes.rationale: If a judge writes prose-wrapped JSON or fails to create its done file, recover the outer object into the queue so ingest can retry or continue deterministically.

nodes.label: Bench-Bug Zero-Axis Invariant
nodes.rationale: A bench-bug judgment is valid only when every axis and overall are exactly zero, keeping harness failures out of quality means.

nodes.label: MLX Memory Safety Controls
nodes.rationale: Preflight headroom rejects unsafe candidates, while a live sampler can latch a breach and kill the server before host OOM.

nodes.label: Unified Local and Cloud Benchmark Path
nodes.rationale: The local runner invokes the same rundale_bench.py orchestrator used for cloud targets instead of duplicating grading logic.
nodes.norm_label: unified local and cloud benchmark path

nodes.label: Hugging Face Candidate Preflight
nodes.rationale: Multimodal repositories and repositories without a chat template are rejected because text-only mlx_lm serving or raw prompt formatting would produce invalid benchmark evidence.

nodes.label: Score-Gated Tier Promotion Funnel
nodes.rationale: Promotion requires both an overall threshold and every dialogue axis above its floor, with explicit include and exclude overrides.

nodes.label: Sonnet-Only Judge Chokepoint
nodes.rationale: Every judge-loading path refuses non-Claude-subagent, non-Sonnet-4.6, or API-key-bearing configurations.

nodes.label: Pending-Judge Null Semantics
nodes.rationale: When bundles remain unjudged, score fields become null and pending_judge is set so incomplete results cannot masquerade as real zero scores.

nodes.label: Multi-Turn Judge V2 Configuration

nodes.label: Reaction Judge V1 Configuration

nodes.label: Simulation Judge V1 Configuration

nodes.label: Dialogue Judge V1 Configuration

nodes.label: Dialogue Judge V2 Configuration
nodes.rationale: V2 generalizes dialogue judging to any NPC, adds brevity, repetition, mood fidelity, and grounding, defines weighted overall scoring, and preserves v1 as an immutable historical rubric.

nodes.label: Six-Axis Multi-Turn Judge Contract

nodes.label: Reaction Persona Judge Contract

nodes.label: Background Simulation Plausibility Contract
